doc.title: iTJSDispatch2 Interface
doc.para:
What is iTJSDispatch2 iTJSDispatch2 is an abstract base class that provides an interface for "objects" in TJS2. "Objects" in TJS2 include function objects, classes, property objects, arrays (dictionary arrays), etc. Most operations in TJS2 can be performed through this interface.
Below, the description is provided from the perspective of using this interface.

Calls by Ordinal Number
Some methods of iTJSDispatch2 have names ending in ByNum. These perform calls by ordinal number; for example, calling FuncCall with "23" as the member name is equivalent to calling FuncCallByNum with 23 as the ordinal. This will be useful when accessing array objects.
Methods ending in ByNum do not have the membername and hint arguments of their non-ByNum counterparts, but instead have tjs_int num. Specify the ordinal number in the num argument.
Detailed explanations for methods performing calls by ordinal number are omitted below (please refer to the explanations for the corresponding methods without ByNum).

AddRef tjs_uint iTJSDispatch2::AddRef(void)
Increments the object's reference counter. Each object in TJS2 is managed by a reference counter. The return value is the value of the reference counter after incrementing, but relying on this value is not recommended.

Release tjs_uint iTJSDispatch2::Release(void)
Decrements the object's reference counter. The return value is the value of the reference counter after decrementing; returning 0 indicates that the object was freed. However, relying on this value is not recommended.

FuncCall tjs_error iTJSDispatch2::FuncCall( tjs_uint32 flag, const tjs_char * membername, tjs_uint32 *hint, tTJSVariant *result, tjs_int numparams, tTJSVariant **param, iTJSDispatch2 *objthis )
Performs a function call.
The arguments are as follows:
tjs_uint32 flag
Call flags (see below).
const tjs_char * membername
The name of the member to be operated on. If NULL, the operation is on this object itself. In this case, this object must have function capabilities.
tjs_uint32 *hint
Specifies the variable region for storing a "hint". Can be NULL. Hints are meant to speed up subsequent searches for the same member name. If a pointer to a tjs_uint32 variable is specified for hint, a numerical hint value will be written there. Subsequent searches use this number as a reference. Since it is only used as a reference, the initial value of the hint can be any value (0 is recommended). Also, because of this mechanism, it is more efficient if there is a one-to-one correspondence between hints and member names (the tTJSString type has a mechanism for this hint). Depending on the object, it may not have a mechanism to utilize hints.
tTJSVariant *result
Specifies a pointer to a tTJSVariant type to store the result of the function call. If the result is not needed, NULL may be specified.
tjs_int numparams
Specifies the number of arguments passed to the function.
tTJSVariant **param
Passes an array of pointers to arguments passed to the function. If there are no arguments, NULL may be used.
iTJSDispatch2 *objthis
Specifies the context (this object) in which the function is executed.

FuncCallByNum tjs_error iTJSDispatch2::FuncCall( tjs_uint32 flag, tjs_int num, tTJSVariant *result, tjs_int numparams, tTJSVariant **param, iTJSDispatch2 *objthis )
Performs a function call by ordinal number.

PropGet tjs_error iTJSDispatch2::PropGet( tjs_uint32 flag, const tjs_char * membername, tjs_uint32 *hint, tTJSVariant *result, iTJSDispatch2 *objthis )
Retrieves the value of a property or member variable.
The arguments are as follows:
tjs_uint32 flag
Call flags (see below).
const tjs_char * membername
The name of the member to be operated on.
If NULL, the operation is on this object itself. In this case, this object must have property retrieval capabilities. An object that succeeds even when this argument is NULL is considered a property object. Normally, when such a property object becomes a member of another object, the result of executing PropGet on that property object is used instead of the property object itself. This behavior can be bypassed by specifying TJS_IGNOREPROP in the call flags.
tjs_uint32 *hint
Specifies the variable region for storing a hint. Can be NULL. For an explanation of hints, please refer to the explanation for FuncCall.
tTJSVariant *result
Specifies a pointer to a tTJSVariant type to store the result. NULL is not allowed.
iTJSDispatch2 *objthis
Specifies the context (this object) in which this method is executed.

PropGetByNum tjs_error iTJSDispatch2::PropGetByNum( tjs_uint32 flag, tjs_int num, tTJSVariant *result, iTJSDispatch2 *objthis )
Retrieves the value of a property or member variable by ordinal number.

PropSet tjs_error iTJSDispatch2::PropSet( tjs_uint32 flag, const tjs_char *membername, tjs_uint32 *hint, const tTJSVariant *param, iTJSDispatch2 *objthis )
Sets the value of a property or member variable.
The arguments are as follows:
tjs_uint32 flag
Call flags (see below).
const tjs_char * membername
The name of the member to be operated on.
If NULL, the operation is on this object itself. In this case, this object must have property setting capabilities. An object that succeeds even when this argument is NULL is considered a property object. Normally, when such a property object becomes a member of another object, PropSet is called on that property object instead of the property object itself. This behavior can be bypassed by specifying TJS_IGNOREPROP in the call flags.
tjs_uint32 *hint
Specifies the variable region for storing a hint. Can be NULL. For an explanation of hints, please refer to the explanation for FuncCall.
const tTJSVariant *param
Specifies a pointer to a tTJSVariant variable representing the value to be set. NULL is not allowed.
iTJSDispatch2 *objthis
Specifies the context (this object) in which this method is executed.

PropSetByVS tjs_error iTJSDispatch2::PropSetByVS( tjs_uint32 flag, tTJSVariantString *membername, const tTJSVariant *param, iTJSDispatch2 *objthis )
Sets the value of a property or member variable. It differs from PropSet in that the member name is referenced via tTJSVariantString. Used internally. Since tTJSVariantString has a mechanism where multiple string objects share the same memory area for strings, setting properties (creating members within an object) via this method can prevent an increase in memory used for string memory areas for member names. If this method is not implemented, return TJS_E_NOTIMPL. PropSet will be used instead. Also, if calling this method returns TJS_E_NOTIMPL, implement logic to use PropSet instead.

PropSetByNum tjs_error iTJSDispatch2::PropSetByNum( tjs_uint32 flag, tjs_int num, const tTJSVariant *param, iTJSDispatch2 *objthis )
Sets the value of a property or member variable by ordinal number.

GetCount tjs_error iTJSDispatch2::GetCount( tjs_int *result, const tjs_char *membername, tjs_uint32 *hint, iTJSDispatch2 *objthis )
Returns the number of members held by the object.
The arguments are as follows:
tjs_int *result
Specifies a pointer to a variable to store the result. NULL is not allowed.
const tjs_char * membername
Specifies the name of the target member. If NULL, returns the number of members held by this object itself. If a member name is specified, if that member is an object, returns the number of members held by that object. Fails if the specified member is not of object type.
tjs_uint32 *hint
Specifies the variable region for storing a hint. Can be NULL. For an explanation of hints, please refer to the explanation for FuncCall.
iTJSDispatch2 *objthis
Specifies the context (this object) in which this method is executed. This argument usually has no meaning (it is ignored).

GetCountByNum tjs_error iTJSDispatch2::GetCount( tjs_int *result, tjs_int num, iTJSDispatch2 *objthis )
Ordinal version of GetCount.

DeleteMember tjs_error iTJSDispatch2::DeleteMember( tjs_uint32 flag, const tjs_char *membername, tjs_uint32 *hint, iTJSDispatch2 *objthis )
Deletes a member.
The arguments are as follows:
tjs_uint32 flag
Call flags (see below).
const tjs_char * membername
Specifies the name of the target member. NULL is not allowed.
tjs_uint32 *hint
Specifies the variable region for storing a hint. Can be NULL. For an explanation of hints, please refer to the explanation for FuncCall.
iTJSDispatch2 *objthis
Specifies the context (this object) in which this method is executed. This argument usually has no meaning (it is ignored).

DeleteMemberByNum tjs_error iTJSDispatch2::DeleteMemberByNum( tjs_uint32 flag, tjs_int num, iTJSDispatch2 *objthis )
Deletes a member by ordinal number.

EnumMembers tjs_error iTJSDispatch2::EnumMembers( tjs_uint32 flag, tTJSVariantClosure *callback, iTJSDispatch2 *objthis )
Enumerates members within the object. A callback function can be specified in callback, but in the current version, behavior when creating or deleting members of this object within the callback function is not guaranteed.
The arguments are as follows:
tjs_uint32 flag
Call flags. Specify the bitwise OR of the flags below, or 0 (zero).
TJS_IGNOREPROP
Disables property access. When enumerating members and retrieving values, if this flag is specified and a member is a property, the property object itself is obtained. If this flag is not specified, the value obtained through the property object is obtained.
TJS_ENUM_NO_VALUE
Does not retrieve values. If this flag is specified, 2 arguments are passed to the callback function. If not specified, 3 arguments are passed.
tTJSVariantClosure *callback
Specifies the callback function. This callback function has callback->FuncCall invoked once for each member. Two arguments (when TJS_ENUM_NO_VALUE is specified) or three arguments (when TJS_ENUM_NO_VALUE is not specified) are passed to the function.
The 1st argument is string type, representing the member name
The 2nd argument is integer type, representing flags for that member. A bitwise OR combination of TJS_HIDDENMEMBER or TJS_STATICMEMBER, or 0 is specified
The 3rd argument exists only when TJS_ENUM_NO_VALUE is not specified, and represents the value of that member
iTJSDispatch2 *objthis
Specifies the context (this object) in which this method is executed. If the TJS_IGNOREPROP flag is not specified, this argument becomes the default context in which property objects are executed.

Invalidate tjs_error iTJSDispatch2::Invalidate( tjs_uint32 flag, const tjs_char *membername, tjs_uint32 *hint, iTJSDispatch2 *objthis )
Performs invalidation.
The arguments are as follows:
tjs_uint32 flag
Call flags (see below).
const tjs_char * membername
Specifies the name of the target member. If NULL, this object itself is invalidated. If a member name is specified, if that member is an object, that object is invalidated. Fails if the specified member is not of object type.
tjs_uint32 *hint
Specifies the variable region for storing a hint. Can be NULL. For an explanation of hints, please refer to the explanation for FuncCall.
iTJSDispatch2 *objthis
Specifies the context (this object) in which this method is executed. This argument usually has no meaning (it is ignored).

InvalidateByNum tjs_error iTJSDispatch2::InvalidateByNum( tjs_uint32 flag, tjs_int num, iTJSDispatch2 *objthis )
Performs invalidation by ordinal number.

IsValid tjs_error iTJSDispatch2::IsValid( tjs_uint32 flag, const tjs_char *membername, tjs_uint32 *hint, iTJSDispatch2 *objthis )
Checks whether an object is valid. Returns TJS_S_TRUE if valid, or TJS_S_FALSE if invalid.
The arguments are as follows:
tjs_uint32 flag
Call flags (see below).
const tjs_char * membername
Specifies the name of the target member. If NULL, checks the validity of this object itself. If a member name is specified, if that member is an object, checks the validity of that object. Fails if the specified member is not of object type.
tjs_uint32 *hint
Specifies the variable region for storing a hint. Can be NULL. For an explanation of hints, please refer to the explanation for FuncCall.
iTJSDispatch2 *objthis
Specifies the context (this object) in which this method is executed. This argument usually has no meaning (it is ignored).

IsValidByNum tjs_error iTJSDispatch2::IsValidByNum( tjs_uint32 flag, tjs_int num, iTJSDispatch2 *objthis )
Checks whether an object is valid by ordinal number.

Deletes a member.
The arguments are as follows:
tjs_uint32 flag
Call flags (see below).
const tjs_char * membername
Specifies the name of the target member. NULL is not allowed.
tjs_uint32 *hint
Specifies the variable region for storing a hint. Can be NULL. For an explanation of hints, please refer to the explanation for FuncCall.

Specifies the context (this object) in which this method is executed. This argument usually has no meaning (it is ignored).

EnumMembers tjs_error iTJSDispatch2::EnumMembers( tjs_uint32 flag, tTJSVariantClosure *callback, iTJSDispatch2 *objthis )
Enumerates members within the object. A callback function can be specified in callback, but in the current version, behavior when creating or deleting members of this object within the callback function is not guaranteed.
The arguments are as follows:
tjs_uint32 flag
Call flags. Specify the bitwise OR of the flags below, or 0 (zero).
TJS_IGNOREPROP
Disables property access. When enumerating members and retrieving values, if this flag is specified and a member is a property, the property object itself is obtained. If this flag is not specified, the value obtained through the property object is obtained.
TJS_ENUM_NO_VALUE
Does not retrieve values. If this flag is specified, 2 arguments are passed to the callback function. If not specified, 3 arguments are passed.
tTJSVariantClosure *callback
Specifies the callback function. This callback function has callback->FuncCall invoked once for each member. Two arguments (when TJS_ENUM_NO_VALUE is specified) or three arguments (when TJS_ENUM_NO_VALUE is not specified) are passed to the function.
The 1st argument is string type, representing the member name
The 2nd argument is integer type, representing flags for that member. A bitwise OR combination of TJS_HIDDENMEMBER or TJS_STATICMEMBER, or 0 is specified
The 3rd argument exists only when TJS_ENUM_NO_VALUE is not specified, and represents the value of that member

Specifies the context (this object) in which this method is executed. If the TJS_IGNOREPROP flag is not specified, this argument becomes the default context in which property objects are executed.

Performs invalidation.
The arguments are as follows:
tjs_uint32 flag
Call flags (see below).
const tjs_char * membername
Specifies the name of the target member. If NULL, this object itself is invalidated. If a member name is specified, if that member is an object, that object is invalidated. Fails if the specified member is not of object type.
tjs_uint32 *hint
Specifies the variable region for storing a hint. Can be NULL. For an explanation of hints, please refer to the explanation for FuncCall.
iTJSDispatch2 *objthis
Specifies the context (this object) in which this method is executed. This argument usually has no meaning (it is ignored).

The arguments are as follows:
tjs_uint32 flag
Call flags (see below).
const tjs_char * membername
Specifies the name of the target member. If NULL, checks the validity of this object itself. If a member name is specified, if that member is an object, checks the validity of that object. Fails if the specified member is not of object type.
tjs_uint32 *hint
Specifies the variable region for storing a hint. Can be NULL. For an explanation of hints, please refer to the explanation for FuncCall.

CreateNew tjs_error iTJSDispatch2::CreateNew( tjs_uint32 flag, const tjs_char * membername, tjs_uint32 *hint, iTJSDispatch2 **result, tjs_int numparams, tTJSVariant **param, iTJSDispatch2 *objthis )
Creates a new object. Similar to the FuncCall method, this method can accept arguments for creating a new object. So-called "class objects" that serve as templates for objects must implement this method.
The arguments are as follows:
tjs_uint32 flag
Call flags (see below).
const tjs_char * membername
The name of the member to be operated on. If NULL, the operation is on this object itself. In this case, this object must have capabilities to create new objects.
tjs_uint32 *hint
Specifies the variable region for storing a hint. Can be NULL. For an explanation of hints, please refer to the explanation for FuncCall.
iTJSDispatch2 **result
Specifies a pointer to an iTJSDispatch* type to store the newly created object. NULL is not allowed.
tjs_int numparams
Specifies the number of arguments passed when creating a new object.
tTJSVariant **param
Passes an array of pointers to arguments passed when creating a new object. If there are no arguments, NULL may be used.
iTJSDispatch2 *objthis
Specifies the context (this object) executed when creating a new object.

CreateNewByNum tjs_error iTJSDispatch2::CreateNew( tjs_uint32 flag, tjs_int num, iTJSDispatch2 **result, tjs_int numparams, tTJSVariant **param, iTJSDispatch2 *objthis )
Creates a new object by ordinal number.

IsInstanceOf tjs_error iTJSDispatch2::IsInstanceOf( tjs_uint32 flag, const tjs_char * membername, tjs_uint32 *hint, const tjs_char * classname, iTJSDispatch2 *objthis )
Checks whether an object is an instance of a specific class. The class name is passed as a string in the classname argument. Referenced by the TJS2 instanceof operator. Upon success, returns TJS_S_TRUE if it is an instance of the specified class, or TJS_S_FALSE if not.
The arguments are as follows:
tjs_uint32 flag
Call flags (see below).
const tjs_char * membername
The name of the member to be operated on. If NULL, the operation is on this object itself. In this case, this object must have capabilities to create new objects.
tjs_uint32 *hint
Specifies the variable region for storing a hint. Can be NULL. For an explanation of hints, please refer to the explanation for FuncCall.
const tjs_char *classname
Specifies the class name as a string.
iTJSDispatch2 *objthis
Specifies the context (this object) executed when creating a new object.

IsInstanceOfByNum tjs_error iTJSDispatch2::IsInstanceOfByNum( tjs_uint32 flag, tjs_int num, const tjs_char * classname, iTJSDispatch2 *objthis )
Checks whether an object is an instance of a specific class by ordinal number.

Operation tjs_error iTJSDispatch2::Operation( tjs_uint32 flag, const tjs_char *membername, tjs_uint32 *hint, tTJSVariant *result, const tTJSVariant *param, iTJSDispatch2 *objthis )
Performs an operation on a member. The type of operation is specified by flag.
The arguments are as follows:
tjs_uint32 flag
Call flags. In addition to normal call flags below, one of the following flags must be added via bitwise OR to specify the operation type.
Note that in this explanation, v represents the member's value and p represents the parameter passed in the param argument.
TJS_OP_BAND
Bitwise AND operation v &= p
TJS_OP_BOR
Bitwise OR operation v |= p
TJS_OP_BXOR
Bitwise XOR operation v ^= p
TJS_OP_SUB
Subtraction v -= p
TJS_OP_ADD
Addition v += p
TJS_OP_MOD
Modulo v %= p
TJS_OP_DIV
Real number division v /= p
TJS_OP_IDIV
Integer division v \= p
TJS_OP_MUL
Multiplication v *= p
TJS_OP_LOR
Logical OR v = v || p
TJS_OP_LAND
Logical AND v = v && p
TJS_OP_SAR
Arithmetic right shift v >>= p
TJS_OP_SAL
Arithmetic left shift v <<= p
TJS_OP_SR
Bitwise right shift v >>>= p
TJS_OP_INC
Increment v++ The param argument is ignored
TJS_OP_DEC
Decrement v-- The param argument is ignored
const tjs_char * membername
The name of the member to be operated on. NULL is not allowed.
tjs_uint32 *hint
Specifies the variable region for storing a hint. Can be NULL. For an explanation of hints, please refer to the explanation for FuncCall.
tTJSVariant *result
Specifies a pointer to a tTJSVariant variable to store the result of the operation. May be NULL.
tTJSVariant *param
Specifies parameters for the operation. May be NULL if TJS_OP_INC or TJS_OP_DEC is specified as the operation type.
iTJSDispatch2 *objthis
Specifies the context in which the operation is executed, but is usually ignored.

NativeInstanceSupport tjs_error iTJSDispatch2::NativeInstanceSupport( tjs_uint32 flag, tjs_int32 classid, iTJSNativeInstance **pointer )
Associates native code instances with an object, or retrieves native code instances from an object.
The arguments are as follows:
tjs_uint32 flag
Specifies call flags. Must specify one of the following values:
TJS_NIS_REGISTER
Registers the native code instance indicated by *pointer. Uses classid to identify the native code class.
TJS_NIS_GETINSTANCE
Writes the native code instance with the class ID specified by classid into *pointer.
tjs_int32 classid
Specifies the class ID of native code. TJSRegisterNativeClass, TJSFindNativeClassID, and TJSFindNativeClassName can be used to manage native code class IDs, but usually these processes are automatically handled by helper code for writing native code (described in tjsNative.cpp/tjsNative.h).
iTJSNativeInstance **pointer
Specifies a pointer to an iTJSNativeInstance* type variable in order to pass or receive native code instances.

ClassInstanceInfo tjs_error iTJSDispatch2::ClassInstanceInfo( tjs_uint32 flag, tjs_uint num, tTJSVariant *value )
Method that manipulates class instance information used by the IsInstanceOf method. Class names can be added to identify which class an object is an instance of, or classes can be enumerated to check which class an object is an instance of.
The arguments are as follows:
tjs_uint32 flag
Call flags. Specify one of the following flags:
TJS_CII_ADD
Adds instance information. Passes a pointer to a tTJSVariant variable storing the class name (string) in value. The num argument is ignored.
TJS_CII_GET
Retrieves instance information. Specifies an integer starting from 0 for the num argument. Returning TJS_E_FAIL occurs if num exceeds the number of set instance information items. Passes a pointer to a tTJSVariant variable to receive the class name in value.
tjs_uint num
Specifies the ordinal number when TJS_CII_GET is specified for flag.
tTJSVariant *value
When TJS_CII_ADD is specified for flag, passes a pointer to a tTJSVariant variable storing the class name. When TJS_CII_GET is specified for flag, passes a pointer to a tTJSVariant variable to receive the class name.

Call Flags
Call flags. A combination of the following values using bitwise OR can be specified:
TJS_MEMBERENSURE
Forces creation of a member if the specified member name is not found. Valid as a call flag for PropSet. )
TJS_MEMBERMUSTEXIST
Causes an error if the specified member name is not found. This is valid for objects like Dictionary or Array that return void by default when a member is not found (for objects that are not of this type, a missing member results in an error by default).
TJS_IGNOREPROP
Bypasses property operations. Normally, in TJS2 objects, if a specified member is an object and PropSet or PropGet succeeds on that object (in the case of a property object), the result of PropSet or PropGet on that member is used instead of that member itself. Specifying this flag bypasses such processing, so even if the specified member is a property object, the operation is performed on the property object itself.
TJS_HIDDENMEMBER
Creating a member with this flag specified makes the member invisible. Depending on the object, it may not be supported.
TJS_STATICMEMBER
Creating a member with this flag specified makes the member static (independent of execution context). Depending on the object, it may not be supported.

tjs_error tjs_error is the error type returned by each method of iTJSDispatch2 (except AddRef and Release). It takes the following values. Also, for values not listed here, if the value is negative, it must be considered an error. To determine these, the TJS_SUCCEEDED and TJS_FAILED macros can be used.
TJS_E_MEMBERNOTFOUND
The specified member was not found.
TJS_E_NOTIMPL
The function attempting to be called is not implemented.
TJS_E_INVALIDPARAM
Invalid argument.
TJS_E_BADPARAMCOUNT
Invalid number of arguments.
TJS_E_INVALIDTYPE
Not a function, or the property type is different. This value is returned when trying to call something that is not a function, or attempting to treat something that is not a property as a property.
TJS_E_INVALIDOBJECT
The object has already been invalidated.
TJS_E_ACCESSDENYED
Attempted an operation that cannot be performed on a read-only or write-only property.
TJS_E_NATIVECLASSCRASH
Execution context is different. This value is returned when trying to execute a method implemented in native code in a context that cannot be handled by that native code (such as on an object of a different class).
TJS_S_TRUE
Not an error, but indicates that the result is "true".
TJS_S_FALSE
Not an error, but indicates that the result is "false".
TJS_S_OK
Normally returned when no error occurred.
TJS_E_FAIL
Returned when an undefined error occurs.
TJS_FAILED(x)
Macro that evaluates to true if x is an error value.
TJS_SUCCEEDED(x)
Macro that evaluates to true if x is a non-error value.
Error definitions and related macros are described in tjsErrorDef.h. Also, runtime exceptions (in C++) may be thrown instead of returning errors. Sufficient consideration must be given to runtime exceptions during programming.
